passage:
In recent years, zero-waste grocery stores have opened in many cities. In these shops, food like rice, nuts, and pasta is sold in large bins with no packaging. Customers bring their own jars, bags, or containers and fill them with only what they need. Many people see these stores as a simple way to cut down on plastic waste.

Supporters say zero-waste stores help people think about how much garbage they create. At a regular supermarket, most food comes in plastic bags, boxes, or wrappers that go straight into the trash. At a zero-waste store, shoppers can see how much they are saving by reusing their own containers. Some customers also say they waste less food, because they can buy exactly the amount they need. For supporters, shopping this way is a small habit that makes a real difference.

However, not everyone agrees. Critics say the stores are not practical for most families. Shoppers have to clean their containers, carry them to the store, and have them weighed before filling them. This takes extra time, which busy parents and workers may not have. Prices are also often higher than at regular supermarkets, and many zero-waste stores are in wealthier neighbourhoods. Some people also worry about food safety. Packaging keeps food fresh and clean, and open bins can get dirty if they are not looked after carefully.

Other critics believe that the real problem is not shoppers but the big companies that make plastic packaging. They say it would be better to ask the government to make stricter rules for these companies than to ask ordinary people to change their shopping habits.

Even so, many people agree that zero-waste stores have started an important conversation. Some regular supermarkets have already begun offering refill stations and using less packaging. The challenge now is to find ways that make waste reduction easy and affordable for everyone.
